Replay

Replay: an experimental simulation-first library

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
The contractPresent limitsOptional exact correction reuse

Replay explores a multiplayer authoring model built around a complete, replayable Odin world. It lives beside Kit and uses none of Kit's replication, simulation, or session runtime. Both implementations and both versions of each ported game must remain available.

Replay implements local simulation, server-authoritative prediction/reconciliation, cooperative owner streams, and deterministic P2P rollback. Its shared foundations include bounded typed history, entity pools/RNG, canonical codecs, presentation journals, recipient views, checkpoints, durable enrollment and host migration. Godot owns scenes/input/output; the simulation packages run without Godot.

Start with getting started, the Session starter project, and the checked lifecycle recipes. Most games need one Timeline, Session or Room owner; the package reference below includes advanced mechanisms and tools, not a checklist of required imports. Kit (v1) and Replay (v2) share Odin/API conventions while retaining their different gameplay models.

The library remains experimental. Use the framework completion audit to distinguish implemented contracts, tested combinations and remaining framework work. Full parity across every ported game is not its completion gate.

From the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_view/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_loot/run.sh

The test gate runs native tests, type-checks the instantiated example for WASM, and executes the example. It is also registered in tests/run_all.sh.

The contract#

Odin
import replay "godot:replay"

World :: struct {position: i32, rng: replay.Rng}
Input :: struct {move: i8}
Event :: struct {position: i32}

step :: proc(world: ^World, input: Input, ctx: ^replay.Step(Event)) {
    world.position += i32(input.move)
}

// Application initialization:
timeline: replay.Timeline(World, Input, Event)
err := replay.init(&timeline, replay.Frame(World){}, step)
// Check err, advance with typed inputs, copy frames for presentation, and destroy.

Store all mutable gameplay state in World, including RNG, cooldowns, scheduled work, entity lifetime, and entity allocation. A step can modify several entities directly. Read device input before calling advance. Draw from copies returned by current or read; presentation never writes into simulation.

The value-storage implementation supports scalars, enums, bit sets, fixed arrays, ordinary structs and supported tagged unions containing those values. Initialization recursively rejects pointers, slices, strings, maps, procedures, and other unsupported types. Struct padding is allowed: these are typed, same-process snapshots, not wire packets. Canonical wire codecs live in replay/schema; dynamic collections remain future storage work.

Treat a live Timeline as a single owner of allocations: keep it in one place, pass it by pointer, and call destroy once. Frame and event reads return/copy owned values. Pool pointers and step contexts are borrowed for the current step.

Present limits#

  • Room has native/browser planned/crash migration, returned-host, repeated-handoff, control-partition and successor-loss evidence. Owner-driven co-op and native/ browser P2P have separate contracts. These tests establish bounded scenarios, not arbitrary public reachability or platform coverage. Steam has contract tests; live-account acceptance remains separate.
  • Server snapshots use acknowledged deltas, negotiated compression and full-state recovery. Prediction groups and recipient views are authored policies: the framework validates their declared invariants, not arbitrary gameplay dependencies.
  • revise_input supplies an explicitly corrected input batch; it is not a network protocol and does not decide whose input or state is authoritative.
  • Initializing another timeline from a saved Frame proves in-process resume. Its epoch only scopes event IDs; it does not elect a host or reject packets.
  • Events have speculative/confirmed/watched presentation and cancellation/update delivery. Committed external effects/outboxes remain future work. Do not play effects directly from a step.
  • audit reports the first differing tick. audit_capture retains the exact mismatch; canonical schema diagnostics identify differing fields. Local audit does not prove arbitrary game code deterministic across platforms. P2P has separate recorded-corpus cross-target checks.
  • Whole frames and replay scratch are copied. This deliberately prioritizes correctness while the API is explored; scale claims require measurements.

The API is experimental. The framework audit and each package's tested envelope determine what can be described as supported; historical game parity ledgers do not imply missing framework features.

Optional exact correction reuse#

correct_reusing(timeline, truth, events[, rewrite]) returns the ordinary Result and a separate reused-record count. It validates the same checkpoint/event/history conditions as correct, calls the rewriter for every visited suffix input, and publishes atomically. When the complete predecessor state and rewritten input are byte-identical to their recorded counterparts, the existing record is retained; its state/events need no simulation or copying. Changed inputs and state continue through normal simulation, and reuse may resume after exact convergence.

This requires a deterministic step with all mutable dependencies in State/Input and unchanged external configuration/callbacks. It is explicit and opt-in. Padding may conservatively prevent reuse; byte comparison also distinguishes signed zero. The ordinary correct and audit paths still execute the whole suffix. Audit never trusts reused records as proof of determinism. Result.steps remains the processed suffix span; subtract the separately returned count for simulated correction steps. A failed call returns zero reuse and leaves published state/input/events unchanged.
